source_text: What's going on with the 2 to 2.5 hour probe??  I tohught things were going to be fast now

fragments.text: What's going on with the 2 to 2.5 hour probe??
I tohught things were going to be fast now

reply_text:
㊥ (why the probe takes 2.5 hours) Two reasons. First, the speed-ups we tried today didn't pan out, so a cold probe still takes 10–60 minutes per row under this load. Second, my mistake made it worse: I asked claude-3 for an empty cache per row on a re-probe whose only purpose is to sort rows by their new stops. An empty cache per row is for accepting a fix. For a re-probe at a fixed compiler, a warm cache is valid and much faster. I've just told claude-3 to switch, keeping the rows already running: each lane builds its cache once and reuses it, so later rows should take minutes. claude-3 will send a new estimate.

㊟ (what is and isn't fast now)
- **Fast:** reruns at an unchanged compiler, like this re-probe or discovery traces. These take seconds to a few minutes once the cache is warm.
- **Still slow:** anything after editing the compiler. Every fix still pays one full cold build, 15–40 minutes. Warm-after-edit was slower than cold, the inventory cache saved nothing, and selective invalidation would need a much larger redesign to be safe.
- **Credits:** the polling rule and fresh sessions cut agents' waiting costs, but they don't shorten the builds themselves.

㊟ (one risk with warm caches) Earlier today we saw that a cache built by one row can occasionally change another row's verdict. So claude-3 will rerun cold any row whose new stop looks surprising before reporting it.

(the merge)
- **Push setting.** Origin push stays disabled. I'll treat your instruction as permission for that one merge-and-push, as I did for the notes branch.

- **Rob's branch.** cand-1 is based on Rob's history up to our pin. I'll check how far `origin/main` has moved and merge it in first if needed, so `main` gets a clean merge.
